mission_01: Excellent work implementing the complete MFCC extraction pipeline! You now understand how raw audio waveforms are transformed into compact feature representations that capture the perceptually relevant aspects of speech. The pre-emphasis filter compensates for the natural spectral tilt of speech, the Hamming window minimizes spectral leakage at frame boundaries, and the mel filter bank mimics the human ear's frequency resolution. The logarithm compresses the wide dynamic range of speech energies, and the DCT produces uncorrelated coefficients that are ideal for statistical modeling. MFCCs remain the foundational feature representation for speech recognition, serving as input to everything from Gaussian Mixture Models to modern deep neural networks. Understanding this pipeline gives you insight into why certain audio processing choices are made and how they affect downstream recognition performance.
